A .fai row has 5 TAB-separated columns (6 for FASTQ), all numbers after NAME.
A BGZF file ends with the 28-byte end-of-file block.
A BGZF file is a series of gzip members, each carrying the `BC` extra subfield.
A FASTA file ends with a newline.
A FASTQ file is not truncated: its last record is complete.
A FASTQ record's quality string is exactly as long as its sequence.
Containers are complete: gzip integrity and the BGZF end-of-file block.
Each FASTQ record starts with a title line beginning with `@`.
Every .fai row reproduces the FASTA's bytes.
Every FASTA header has a non-empty name.
Every sequence line of a record has the same length, except a shorter last line.
Exactly four lines per FASTQ record (no wrapping).
FASTA sequence lines hold no spaces or TABs.
In a .fai row, LINEWIDTH is at least LINEBASES.
Line terminators are consistent within a FASTA record.
No FASTA record is empty.
No FASTQ read has zero length.
One or more sequence lines, then a line starting with `+`.
Quality characters run from `!` to `~`, and sequence lines hold no spaces or TABs.
Quality encoding: Phred+33 unless the characters suggest Phred+64.
Rows follow the FASTA's order, so OFFSET increases down the file.
Sequence characters are IUPAC nucleotide or amino-acid codes.
The `+` line is bare, or repeats the title exactly.
